ra: Al-Aql is the first of the five cosmic luminaries (al-hudud).
Al-Nafs is the second of the five luminaries.
Al-Kalima is the third of the five luminaries.
Al-Sabiq is the fourth of the five luminaries.
Al-Tali is the fifth of the five luminaries.
In Druze cosmology the Universal Soul emanates from the Universal Intellect.
The Word emanates from the Universal Soul in the descending hierarchy of luminaries.
The Preceder emanates from the Word.
The Follower emanates from the Preceder, completing the five ranks.
Hamza ibn Ali is held to be the human manifestation of al-Aql, the Universal Intellect.
Abu Ibrahim al-Tamimi is associated with the rank of al-Nafs.
Muhammad ibn Wahb al-Tamimi is associated with the rank of al-Kalima.
Salama ibn Abd al-Wahhab is associated with the rank of al-Sabiq.
Baha al-Din al-Muqtana is held to be the manifestation of al-Tali, the Follower.
As manifestation of al-Aql, Hamza is the human head of the five luminaries.
As manifestation of al-Tali, al-Muqtana belongs to the five luminaries.
In Druze belief al-Hakim, as divine manifestation, stands above and is served by the five cosmic luminaries.
Hamza authored/transmitted a major portion of the epistles collected in the Rasaʾil al-Hikma.
Al-Muqtana compiled and transmitted many of the epistles of the Rasaʾil al-Hikma.
Hamza systematized and proclaimed the Druze doctrine of tawhid.
Taqammus is an integral doctrine within the Druze tawhid worldview.
Al-Darazi's extremist claims were repudiated by Hamza, who declared him a heretic; the two were rivals in the early daʿwa.
Druze tawhid develops the Islamic affirmation of God's absolute unity (Allah) in a distinctive transcendent direction.
Druze veneration of al-Hakim derives from the Fatimid Ismaili doctrine of the imamate (imamah), radicalized into a claim of divine manifestation.
Druze expectation of the return of al-Hakim and Hamza adapts the Shia doctrine of occultation (ghayba) and awaited return.
The Druze Universal Intellect (al-Aql al-Kulli) is functionally cognate to the Neoplatonic/Gnostic Nous as first emanation, a comparison drawn in scholarship on Ismaili-Druze cosmology.
